title: run-136: A fold only when it releases work — the epoch engine stops paying a suite per landing, and the hub shows landed and adopted
body: **Claim:** When I read a run's record, every fold either made a queued task ready, closed the run, or adopted work that had waited a full suite's length — a plan with no edges folds once, and a task lands on the hub as landed, then adopted, never as needing a human when it doesn't. (elicited)

payload.body: Approach: add a `kataLanded(id)` beside `kataAdopted` in fleet/run-engine.mjs — one `kataCall('metadata', …)` patch with exactly {'work.state':'landed','work.attention':'ok','work.attention_msg':''}, guarded `!row || kataClosed.has(id)` and preceded by `drainKataPosts()`. `settleResult` becomes async: the re-edge branch returns its claim untouched, and on the mergeable branch the epoch is claimed synchronously FIRST (so the epoch instant is unchanged — the global constraint) and the landed patch is awaited after the claim and before the lane folds. `kataAdopted`'s patch object gains 'work.state':'adopted'. payload.body: Approach for task 1 (fold triggers): put a predicate in `claimEpoch` — `released` (a queued task whose every predecessor is adopted or in this pending set), `end` (nothing in flight, nothing folding, nothing ready, nothing pending but these), `aged` (oldest pending result older than `foldAgeMs`), checked in that precedence — and return `{results, why, released}` instead of a bare array so both `driver:wave-adopted` and `driver:wave-blocked` can carry `why`. `foldAgeMs` = `args.foldAgeMs` when finite and >= 0, else `max(60000, baseline.wallMs)` with the clause off until the baseline settles (wall recorded in `settleBaseline`). `settleResult` stamps `landedAt` on each pending result; a lane that waits with results pending races `nextLanding()` against an unref'd timer for the remaining age so it wakes without a landing (M5). The three edited sims pass `foldAgeMs: 0` per scenario to keep their BASE expectations; ready_set's `c1` is re-aimed to one `why: 'end'` epoch.

payload.body:
Examiner (exam for Task 1, fleet/tests/test_run_engine_fold_policy.mjs). Approach I am about to take:

The new sim copies test_run_engine_ready_set.mjs's shape (its own `drive`, `taskOf`, `waitUntil`, canned-worker and `readEvents` helpers, rewritten here — nothing imported from a sibling sim), with `foldAgeMs` passed through `extraArgs`. Seven runs:

- b1: three no-edge tasks X/Y/Z, landings staggered ~600 ms apart, check.sh sleeps 0.2 s so the baseline suite's wall is ~200 ms, NO `foldAgeMs` argument -> exactly one adoption, `why: 'end'`. This is how leg (b) observes 'the threshold is 60000': an engine that used the baseline wall alone (200 ms) would age X out and fold three times.
- b2: the same run with `foldAgeMs: 0` -> the first landing folds, `why: 'aged'`, at least two adoptions. Serves leg (b)'s second half AND leg (c)'s second half (same shape; noted in the file).
- b3: the same run with `foldAgeMs: 'x'` -> the default applies, so one adoption, `why: 'end'` [M2's 'otherwise'].
- c1: three no-edge tasks, `foldAgeMs: 600000` -> exactly one adoption, `tasks` `['X','Y','Z']`, `why: 'end'` [M3].
- d1: A->C, B->C, `foldAgeMs: 600000`, A landing first -> exactly two adoptions; the first is `tasks ['A','B']`, `why: 'released'`, `released: ['C']`, appended only after B's `worker:end`; C's `worker:start` follows it carrying that `headSha`; the second is `tasks: ['C']`, `why: 'end'` [M4].
- d2: A lands at once, B held two seconds, `foldAgeMs: 300` -> A adopted alone, `why: 'aged'`, before B's `worker:end`; and the adoption's `ts` measured against A's `worker:end` `ts` is the timer wake [M4 second half, M5].
- r1: a red epoch (suite red once B.txt exists, reconcile refuses) with `foldAgeMs: 0`, so leg (a)'s sweep is asked of a real `driver:wave-blocked` and not only of adoptions.

Then a sweep over every run for leg (a): every `driver:wave-adopted` / `driver:wave-blocked` carries `why` in {released, end, aged}, and a `released` event's ids are each dispatched after it on that `headSha`.

Legs (f) and (g) are read as text: the contract bullet with the fifth `Run:` line's own region and regex, and the three sibling sims read through names BUILT from fragments (`'test_run_engine_' + stem + '.mjs'`) so no literal matching `test_[a-z0-9_]+\.mjs` appears in the file — the global constraint says a sim names no sibling sim, and leg (g) asks for those three to be read as text; building the name is how both hold.

examiner (exam:2@run-136) — approach for the exam at fleet/tests/test_run_engine_kata_landing.mjs.

One scenario, as the Context asks: the close sim's fake-kata shape copied in (never imported), rig driven with kata: fake.kata and extraArgs: { kataRecord }, two tasks, task 1's reviewer passes and task 2's reviewer blocks.

Two readings worth recording, because a later session would otherwise have to re-derive them from a probe:

1. Leg (a)'s 'after the last comment the driver posted for task 1's worker end' is not observable in the rig as a worker:end comment: the rig passes no eventLog, so the engine's MIRRORED_ENVELOPES subscription (worker:start / worker:end) is never installed and those envelopes reach no comment. What IS observable is the driver's own narration, which appendEvent mirrors directly: a driver: event naming a task posts on that task's issue. So both tasks carry one proofRuns command, which puts a driver:proof-run comment on task 1's issue at its grading — the last comment the driver posts for task 1 before its result settles. Leg (a) pins the landed patch after that comment.

2. 'before any fold adopts it' is pinned on the RUN issue, not the task's: driver:wave-adopted carries no task field, so kataUidFor routes it to the run's uid and it lands as a comment there. Measured order at BASE (fake call log, global): U-1 proof-run comment, U-2 proof-run comment, RUN0 driver:wave-adopted, RUN0 driver:integrated-clean, U-1 adoption patch, U-1 close. The landed patch must sit between task 1's proof-run comment and the wave-adopted comment — that is M1's window, read off the hub in one ordering.

The SessionEnd stamp M1 clears is modelled the way it actually happens: the stub worker writes work.attention needs-human / 'session ended without hand-off' straight into the fake's store when each session ends (the hook's write, not the engine's, so it is not recorded as an engine call and does not bump the revision the fake answers — the fake enforces no If-Match, and the revision leg belongs to the adoption sim, not here).

M2's 'and passes' for the close sim is the Proof's first Run: line, which the driver runs; leg (b) here pins the same patch from the engine's side (sorted keys, once, close with reason done next). The exam names no sibling sim in code. Leg (d) is read in-file the way the second Run: line reads it — the re-edge range, zero occurrences of 'exactly the two flat keys', and the Closes: range naming the three keys in order.

payload.author: exam:1@run-136
payload.body:
Examiner: the exam is in at `fleet/tests/test_run_engine_fold_policy.mjs`, red at BASE (47 assertions fail when collected rather than failed fast; the first is scenario b1's). Every failure reads as the absent implementation — `why=undefined` on the epoch events, three folds where the new rule folds once, `foldAgeMs` absent from the contract bullet and from the three sims. Readings a later session would otherwise have to reconstruct:

1. HOW LEG (b) SEES A NUMBER IT CANNOT READ. The sim cannot ask the engine for its threshold, so it asks what the threshold DOES. Scenario b1 gives the run a `check.sh` that sleeps 0.2 s (so the baseline suite's wall is ~200 ms — the exec seam measures it and asserts >= 150 ms as a precondition, so the leg's premise is a fact of the run and not an assumption) and spaces the three landings 600 ms apart. `Math.max(60000, wall)` folds once; the wall alone (200 ms) would age the first result out and fold three times. That is the whole discriminator, and `'x'` (b3) re-asks it for M2's 'otherwise'.

2. WHY LEG (e) IS READ OFF THE FOLD'S START AND NOT ONLY OFF THE ADOPTION. Measured at BASE: A's epoch is claimed at A's landing, the kernel's first `fold` begins 5 ms after A's `worker:end`, and the ADOPTION lands 211 ms after it — i.e. the fold's own wall (kernel, candidate, suite) is ~206 ms, which is of the same order as the 300 ms `foldAgeMs` the leg names. So `adoption.ts - endA.ts` alone does not separate 'folded at the landing' from 'woke on the timer': both land inside the leg's one-second tolerance. The exam therefore keeps the leg's own check as the CEILING (the adoption is within one second of A's `worker:end` plus 300 ms, while B lands at 2000 ms — so the lane did not wait for B) and puts the FLOOR where the fold's wall cannot mask it: the kernel's first `fold` began at least 250 ms after A's `worker:end`. At BASE that is 5 ms; with the timer it is >= 300 ms. Both halves are M5.

3. LEG (a)'s SWEEP IS ASKED OF A RED EPOCH TOO. M1 names `driver:wave-blocked` in its parenthetical, so the sim drives one scenario (r1) whose epoch goes red — suite red once B.txt exists, reconcile refuses — with `foldAgeMs: 0`, and asserts that event carries `why: 'aged'` like any other claimed epoch. The red-BASELINE park is deliberately not exercised: its `driver:wave-blocked` is not the event of a claimed epoch, and this exam says nothing about it.

4. WHAT LEG (g)'s TEXT READ ACCEPTS. The three sims are RUN by their own `Run:` lines; a sim may not run a sibling sim, and their names appear in this file nowhere as a literal (they are built as `'test_run_engine_' + stem + '.mjs'`, so nothing here matches `test_[a-z0-9_]+\.mjs`). What the exam reads is the text. Comments are blanked first — a scenario that merely MENTIONS the knob in prose has not passed it, so writing 'c1 needs no foldAgeMs' in a comment inside c1's call is safe. For each of `a1 a2 b1 b2 d1 d2 e1 e2` it takes the object literal the `tag: '<t>'` sits in — the scenario's own `drive({ … })` argument — and accepts the knob EITHER written there directly OR reached through one level of naming (an identifier in that span bound elsewhere in the file to text mentioning `foldAgeMs`, so a shared `const AGELESS = { foldAgeMs: 0 }` spread into each scenario passes). One level and no further, which is the depth the hermetic probe resolves to; `drive` itself is outside the span, so a default living in the helper is not mistaken for a scenario passing one. `c1` must satisfy NEITHER — it is the scenario re-aimed at the new rule, and the default threshold is what gives it its one `why: 'end'` epoch. The other two sims are asked only for `foldAgeMs: 0` somewhere in their text, which is what the leg says.

5. THE CONTRACT CHECK mirrors the fifth `Run:` line exactly — the same region (the line opening 'The engine's own wave record' through the line opening 'The driver's own executions', four-space indent, joined by spaces) and the same regex — and adds one thing the regex cannot say on its own: M6 asks for the `0` reading as well as the default, so the bullet must carry a standalone `0` (`60000` does not satisfy it).

Sim convention for the peer exam: the literal 'foldAgeMs: 0' sits adjacent to each scenario's 'tag:' in ready_set (a1,a2,b1,b2,d1,d2,e1,e2) so a per-scenario text slice finds it; c1 deliberately passes none and runs on the engine default, which is what makes it a one-epoch why:'end' run. c1's exec-seam hold is gone with it — no scenario holds a fold any more, so the hold plumbing in drive()/kernelSeam() came out.
